title: Cadaver Synod Review — A Sexed-Up Vatican Tragedy and One Hell of a Debut
summary: A four-star review of Ruby Blinkhorn's Cadaver Synod at KXT on Broadway, directed by Mathew Lee. A queer revisionist take on a Vatican scandal that dazzles with wit and craft, even as its final act stumbles.

title: The Whisper Review — Carl Caulfield at Newcastle Civic Playhouse 2026
summary: The Whisper by Carl Caulfield at the Civic Playhouse, Newcastle, UpStage 2026 — a haunted-lodger premise redeemed by idiomatically Australian writing and Matthew McFarlane's magnificent, unsentimental grandfather.

title: lacuna Review — Eric Jiang, Essential Workers at Belvoir Downstairs for Griffin Lookout 2026
summary: Aubrey Wang reviews lacuna by Eric Jiang at Belvoir Downstairs, Griffin Lookout 2026. A freelance psychopomp harvests the memories of the living on contract to the goddess of oblivion. An Orphic English-Cantonese three-hander about queer and diaspora grief, and the gig economy of forgetting.

title: Antigone Review — Gaius Gracchus Society at Chau Chak Wing Museum, University of Sydney 2026
summary: The Gaius Gracchus Society staged Sophocles' Antigone at the Chau Chak Wing Museum, University of Sydney, on 1–2 May 2026. Anastasia Dale finds a production torn between contemporary Australian delivery and classical gravitas — one whose chorus, music, and Madeleine Charters' spellbinding Tiresias point to the show it could have been.

title: Interview · Antigone — James Collins II, Lauren Cleary, Marcel Forrer and Thomas Henderson
summary: The University of Sydney's Classics and Ancient History Society Gaius Gracchus staged three sold-out nights of a full-chorus Antigone from 1–2 May 2026 at the Chau Chak Wing Museum. The project was begun by James Collins II and Daisy Levell. This piece is drawn from written responses by four collaborators — composer-translator-chorister Thomas Henderson, lead choreographer Marcel Forrer, chorus leader Lauren Cleary, and Duncan Eddy-Soros (Creon) — plus an hour-long Zoom with Collins between Sydney and Montreal in July.

title: Interview · Piss Be With You — Cleo Rapture
summary: In Piss Be With You, Cleo Rapture fills a former Baptist tabernacle with an hour of pelvic power, pole and queer inquiry. The one-woman splash-tacular plays Eternity Playhouse for one night only as part of Sydney Fringe 2026.

title: Wallmaxx with me Review — Toni Tait at Artspace, Kudos Live: G R / N D 2026
summary: At Artspace on 6 August, artist Toni Tait sat in an armchair and stared at a plywood wall for two hours, and invited the rest of us to join her. Wallmaxx with me, part of the 2026 Kudos Live: G R / N D showcase, turned a TikTok productivity hack into a collective, public and quietly self-conscious experiment in contemporary boredom — and, more interestingly, in watching others watch a wall.

title: Interview · 50-up: The Rewind — Mary Wyer & Hazel Palmer
summary: In 50-up: The Rewind, a circus cabaret set on the studio floor of Countdown, every performer is over 50. Co-founders Mary Wyer and Hazel Palmer talk ageism, aerials and the not-for-profit they built to give older Australians a way in. At Fool's Paradise, Entertainment Quarter, for Sydney Fringe, 19-20 September.

title: Interview · There's Nothing Funny About Social Work — Ian "Esky" Escandor
summary: In There's Nothing Funny About Social Work, Western Sydney youth worker and stand-up comedian Ian "Esky" Escandor takes a title that sounds like a dare and interrogates it: an hour of comedy about the ethics of visibility and helping people, and if stand-up can provide the support that a support person needs. Directed by Suren Jaemann with dramaturgy by Bina Bhattacharya, at PYT Fairfield, 10–12 September, as part of Sydney Fringe 2026.

title: Interview · In These Shoes — Glynis Traill-Nash
summary: In These Shoes collides the two lives of Glynis Traill-Nash — fashion writer by day, jazz singer by night — into a witty, pacey hour of cabaret. The award-winning show returns to Sydney at Fringe on The Rocks, 2–6 September, after seasons in Perth, Adelaide, Brisbane and the 2025 Edinburgh Fringe.

title: Interview · The Pole Shebang — Andrea James Lui
summary: Andrea James Lui on creating a Fringe show around a lesson plan, clown as an accident, and the small tight-knit village keeping The Pole Shebang upright. Lui brings The Pole Shebang, a coming-of-middle-age story about a nerdy pole teacher late to the biggest, glitziest stage in the land, to Erskineville Town Hall — Emerging Artist Share House for Sydney Fringe, 22–26 September.

title: Interview · The Last Single Girl in Sydney — Nikita Waldron
summary: In The Last Single Girl in Sydney, writer-performer Nikita Waldron plays Poppy, a florist who insists she's fine, she's having fun, and love can't hurt her again. Directed by Maddie Diggins and produced by Peg on a Line Productions, the one-woman show runs 8–12 September at Erskineville Town Hall's Emerging Artist Share House as part of Sydney Fringe 2026.

title: Zoe's Killer Instinct Review — Zoë Jensen at Sydney Fringe 2026
summary: Zoë Jensen's Zoe's Killer Instinct is an extended meditation on power dynamics, misogyny, and what it takes to have that 'killer instinct' — both on and off the stage. Co-created with husband Michael McStay, the darkly comedic cabaret has charming performances and striking costuming, but backs away from the dark themes it addresses and leaves something to be desired. Reviewed by Charlotte Smee.

title: Snow, Moon, and Flowers Review — Sydney Japanese Dance at Sydney Fringe 2026
summary: Sydney Japanese Dance's world premiere Snow, Moon, and Flowers (雪月花) opens a window onto a largely unacknowledged chapter of Australian history, weaving Japanese classical dance, live music, and spoken narrative into a triptych of remembrance. Reviewed at Sydney Fringe Festival on 2 September 2026 by Eugene Blazejowski Walsh — a focused act of remembrance that extends the cherry blossom branch to its audience as an invitation to cultural learning and historical reckoning.

title: Storyteller Review — Melanie Walters at Erskineville Town Hall, Sydney Fringe 2026
summary: Flautist Melanie Walters' solo recital Storyteller at Erskineville Town Hall, part of Sydney Fringe Festival 2026 (1–5 September), weaves contemporary flute works through folktales, poetry and horror films. Angelique Ford finds a virtuosic performer who doesn't just interpret her material but steps inside it — an engaging and technically impressive hour well worth your time.

title: Saltwater Girls Review — Lana Filies at Erskineville Town Hall, Sydney Fringe 2026
summary: Saltwater Girls is for the Catholic girls with a bottomless pit of guilt. It is for those navigating their queerness in an environment where it is to be mocked by peers, a source of discrimination, or something to be surveilled. It’s for anyone who feels like they are yet to or still in the process of figuring how they present themselves to the world. It’s also for anyone who regularly listens to ‘Forgiven’ by Alanis Morissette. Valerie Chidiac reviews Lana Filies’ solo show at Erskineville Town Hall for Sydney Fringe 2026.

title: Epicaricacy Review — Claire Collective Company at The Actors Pulse Playhouse, Sydney Fringe 2026
summary: Valerie Chidiac reviews Claire Collective Company's Epicaricacy, written by and starring Samantha Dewar and directed by Shakira Cheers, at The Actors Pulse Playhouse for Sydney Fringe 2026. A trio of friends in their early twenties — Savannah, Leah and Addy — are pulled apart by peer pressure, substance use, sexual violence and one destabilising Guy. Chidiac finds a piercing study of friendship breakups and gaslighting that centres the trio rather than its interloper.

title: Interview · EPICARICACY — Samantha Dewar & Shakira Cheers
summary: Presented by Claire Collective Company, Samantha Dewar's debut original production Epicaricacy makes its Sydney premiere at Sydney Fringe 2026. A contemporary psychological drama about the fracturing of a young female friendship in the wake of a house party, it plays at The Actors Pulse Playhouse in Redfern from 10 – 12 September. Dewar (writer, producer and performer) and director and stage manager Shakira Cheers spoke with Valerie Chidiac during rehearsals ahead of the season.

title: Interview · The Return — Ala'a Al Qaisi
summary: In The Return, Palestinian‑Jordanian writer‑director Ala'a Al Qaisi stages a father waiting beneath the clouds for his martyred daughters to descend. The play ran 1–3 September at The Greek Theatre at Addi Road as part of Sydney Fringe, and tours to Melbourne and regional Victoria from 15–22 September.
